comment: Foreign downcalls, for the accelerations that have them. Native Image needs every
downcall stub registered ahead of time, and the linker REFUSES the handle for a shape
that has none: one missing entry fails the whole binding -- which both GPU drivers do in
their constructor -- and the binary then declines as though the machine had no device at
all, correct output and silently no acceleration. A downcall entry takes
returnType, parameterTypes and options ONLY; a per-entry "comment" key is rejected by the
schema, which is why the two groups are described here instead.
The objc: package's registration is NOT here: it is its own file,
META-INF/native-image/am.ik.rontolisp/rontolisp-objc/reachability-metadata.json, which this
binary reads as well and the JVM backend copies verbatim into a compiled objc: program
(.kb/objc.md). An image built from the user's jar reads only that jar's META-INF, so the file
stands alone and repeats the shapes it shares with the ones below.
The FIRST THREE are the --native precompile shim's (.kb/native-output.md): rl_precompile
(void*, jlong, void*, void*, void*, void*) -> jint, rl_free (void*, jlong) -> void and
rl_assemble (void*, jlong, void*, jlong, void*, void*) -> jint; its fourth, rl_version
() -> void*, is Metal's MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice shape and registered below.
NativeToolchainTest pins them.
The --blas CBLAS downcalls (.kb/linalg-blas.md) are the next six: two shapes, each at
both widths -- gemm (14 parameters) and gemv (12). gemm is registered twice, because a
product above the critical flop ceiling is issued through the plain
(thread-transitioning) handle instead.
The rest are the CUDA driver API downcalls behind am.ik.gpu (.kb/gpu.md), one entry per
distinct SHAPE rather than per entry point -- 29 handles collapse to 18 signatures, in
the order below:
()                       cuCtxSynchronize
(int)                    cuInit, cuDevicePrimaryCtxRelease_v2
(long)                   cuMemFree_v2
(void*)                  cuCtxSetCurrent, cuDriverGetVersion, cuDeviceGetCount, cuModuleUnload
(void*, int)             cuDeviceGet, cuDevicePrimaryCtxRetain, cuDeviceGetDefaultMemPool
(int, void*)             cuGetErrorString
(void*, long)            cuMemAlloc_v2, cuMemPoolTrimTo
(long, void*)            cuMemFreeAsync
(void*, void*)           cuModuleLoadData, cuMemGetInfo_v2
(void*, int, int)        cuDeviceGetName, cuDeviceGetAttribute
(void*, int, void*)      cuMemPoolSetAttribute, cuMemPoolGetAttribute
(void*, void*, void*)    cuModuleGetFunction
(void*, long, void*)     cuMemAllocAsync
(void*, long, int)       cuMemHostAlloc
(long, void*, long)      cuMemcpyHtoD_v2, critical
(void*, long, long)      cuMemcpyDtoH_v2, critical
(void*, long, long)      cuMemcpyDtoH_v2, plain -- the staged download
(void*, int x7, void* x3) cuLaunchKernel
Both copies are critical: they take a heap segment, so an operand never needs a staging
copy, and one too big for a single critical window is split rather than staged. The
download is ALSO registered plain, for the route that stages it through a pinned buffer.
Regenerate with the tracing agent over a program that opens the binding and runs a
product -- the agent traces Linker.downcallHandle, so constructing CudaDriver or
MetalDriver is enough. The type names are the agent's own (jlong, jint, jboolean);
the un-prefixed aliases parse too, but keeping one spelling keeps a re-run's diff empty.
The LAST 21 are the Metal ones (.kb/gpu.md), and all but one is an objc_msgSend:
one entry per selector SHAPE, since Apple's arm64 rule is that objc_msgSend must be
called through a prototype matching the selector rather than as the variadic it is
declared as. The two-MTLSize-by-value entry is dispatchThreadgroups:threadsPerThreadgroup:,
the widest one is MPSMatrixMultiplication's initWithDevice:..., and the empty one is
MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice, the only C function in the whole binding.
Everything after the Metal ones in the downcalls, and the whole upcalls section, is the ffi:
package's grid (.kb/ffi.md, .kb/cffi.md) -- and it is a GRID, not a table of call sites, because cffi:defcfun invents
shapes at run time, in the user's program, after this binary was built. What makes a finite
registration possible is am.ik.ffi.FfiRuntime's carrier canonicalisation: every narrow
integer argument travels as jlong, every integer return is read as jlong and narrowed by the
declared type, and an ADDRESS is that same jlong -- a pointer and a 64-bit integer are one
parameter on both ABIs the linker serves, so :pointer and :string get no void* of their own.
THREE carriers per parameter. Nothing in the ffi half of either section says void*; the
void* entries above it are the Metal, CUDA and CBLAS bindings (and objc:'s, in its own file), which build their own
descriptors and are not canonicalised. The grid covers, at every return carrier (void,
jlong, jdouble, jfloat): jlong arguments at arity 0-10, all jlong/jdouble combinations at
arity 1-4, and all three carriers at arity 1-2 -- 172 entries, every one with
captureCallState (the errno option every FfiRuntime.call handle carries), plus the two
capture-free shapes the runtime's own constructor binds, malloc's jlong(jlong) and free's
void(jlong). The ffi upcalls are the callback grid: jlong at arity 0-6 and jlong/jdouble at
arity 1-2, at the return carriers void/jlong/jdouble.
The arities are where they are because a registered entry costs image only when it is a
NEW ABI lowering: measured 2026-09-02, pushing jdouble to arity 6 and jfloat to 3 took
this file to 229,386 bytes and the binary from 80,873,736 to 81,332,488 -- ~450KB for
mixed double/pointer calls past arity 4, which is not the shape most C APIs have. Taking
the jlong-only tier from arity 6 to 10 cost nothing at all.
The LAST 810 downcalls are the by-value struct RETURN family. A struct's members are part
of its shape -- they cannot be widened the way an argument is -- so that family is bounded
by member count instead: every member sequence of length 1-2 over the six member layouts
(jbyte, jshort, jint, jlong, jfloat, jdouble) plus the homogeneous ones of length 3-4,
54 return shapes, crossed with 15 parameter tuples (all three carriers at arity 0-2, jlong
at arity 3-4). The ARGUMENTS of such a call still canonicalise, which is what lets the family
reuse those tuples: div, ldiv and imaxdiv are one entry, not three. A struct's padding is part
of its spelling -- the builder rebuilds the layout with MemoryLayout.structLayout, which
REFUSES a member off its own alignment, so a padding-free struct(jbyte,jint) aborts the build
rather than registering anything. Registering a shape is not compiling a stub of its own --
the granularity is the ABI-LOWERED signature, and many descriptors lower the same way: the
3150 entries this family held before the pointer carrier was merged away moved the image by
80 methods and ~30KB of code area, and the binary size and build time not at all (2026-09-02,
GraalVM 25.0.4, Linux x86-64), so what bounds this family is this file, not the image.
A shape outside the grid -- a seventh-plus NARROW integer argument, which keeps its exact
width, a variadic call, a struct ARGUMENT, a struct return past the family's bounds --
SIGNALS in the binary with the one entry that would register it; the JVM registers nothing
ahead of time and binds any shape. The entries are generated from
FfiNativeImageForeignConfigTest's rules (that test pins file and rules against each other),
in its generation order, so a regeneration's diff stays empty.
